top.title: Premier League resumes, Kane facing spell on sidelines: football news – matchday live
top.summary: All the latest match news and buildup for today’s games Today’s games | Tables | Kane injury news | And mail us An email has hit my inbox ‘re the lack of fancy Dan wingers', from Patrick Morgan: I don’t think you’re talking nonsense, but I’d say it’s tactical rather than a lack of talent. Look at Arsenal. Calafiori, Timber and White either bomb on or tuck into midfield, so the wide player has to work more like a No 8, working the half-space and tracking back, rather than being the classic ‘star man’ left high and wide to beat his full-back. Saka is the exception because he does both. A lot of Arsenal’s dynamism doesn’t come from out wide at all. It comes from Declan Rice driving through the middle like a very mobile siege engine. The 2015–2020 lot were mostly given licence to stay forward and decide games, and fewer managers allow that now. It works, but it can make Arsenal a bit stodgy to watch. That being said, I’d instantly forgive Sánchez and take him back over our other options. 60 goals in 120-odd league games, and he could knock out a number on the piano. Phwoar. Continue reading...

latest.title: Light in the dark: 20 long books for short winter days
latest.summary: Turn off your phone, get cosy and commit to some of literature’s biggest and best novels. From Don DeLillo’s Underworld to The Luminaries by Eleanor Catton, these epic reads are worth taking your time over Life starts all over again when it gets crisp in the fall,” wrote F Scott Fitzgerald in The Great Gatsby, and after the beach reads of summer, now feels like the time to settle down to more ambitious projects. Not slim works like Gatsby, but the bigger beasts you have been circling for some time. A book to wrap yourself up in as autumn becomes winter. The year I spent reading The Lord of the Rings when I was eight made me want to be a writer. The novel’s scope and the sheer amount of time I lugged it around with me combined, so that whatever I was doing, part of me was always thinking about it. This is what long books, in particular, can do. Continue reading...

Science.title: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why
Science.summary: Microplastics may be doing something far more dangerous than simply accumulating in our bodies. Scientists have discovered that tiny plastic particles can interact with water to generate highly reactive molecules capable of damaging cells and tissues. This unexpected chemical activity could help explain growing evidence linking microplastic exposure to serious health problems, including heart attacks, strokes, and neurological disorders.

Nearly 50 years after launch, the aging probe continues its historic journey through interstellar space, pushing the limits of human exploration despite dwindling power and technical challenges.

Science.title: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet
Science.summary: A promising material for ultra-fast optical communications has held a secret for decades, but scientists may have finally cracked it. Researchers at KAIST and Caltech have precisely measured how barium titanate controls and absorbs light, resolving longstanding uncertainties that have slowed its development. Their findings could make it easier to build optical devices that transmit information faster while wasting less light.
